steps.title: Why Soliloquies Matter
steps.body: They give direct access to a character's psychology. In "Macbeth," soliloquies show his internal conflict, ambition, guilt, and eventual nihilism.

steps.title: Track language changes
steps.body: How a character speaks at the beginning vs the end shows their development (or deterioration).

steps.title: Shakespeare Language Strategy
steps.body: Focus on three layers: verse form (iambic pentameter, blank verse, prose), imagery patterns (blood, darkness, clothing), and rhetorical devices (repetition, antithesis, soliloquy). When the rhythm breaks, something significant is happening — always ask why. Track how a character's language changes across the play as evidence of development.
